title: User functions: coordinates and results without allocation at the C++/Python boundary
author: Claude-JG
description: revision2026c step RG12.3.1: the user functions take StdVector, which pybind11 maps to numpy, so every call allocates the vectors of its arguments (and its results); for Python functions the call costs more than that, for symbolic user functions it may be the bottleneck. Linking - a numpy array or a symbolic vector that views the C++ memory - is one option; first a pre-analysis: where the allocations happen, what they cost against the call, and what pybind11, numpy and symbolic allow (lifetime, writes, threads). Related: #1864 (MatrixContainer linking a numpy matrix), #1910 (total coordinates linked instead of copied).
releaseNotes: The coordinates and results of user functions pass the C++/Python boundary without allocation: numpy views of the C++ memory as arguments of Python user functions, one copy of a numpy result, and symbolic user functions that evaluate their vector and matrix nodes into their own memory.
